question: Which of the following is a saturated carbon compound?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alkanes are **saturated hydrocarbons** containing only single bonds between carbon atoms (C-C).
 
• The general formula for alkanes is **CₙH₂ₙ₊₂**, where n is the number of carbon atoms.
 
• Examples of alkanes include methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), and propane (C₃H₈).
 
• They are typically less reactive than alkenes and alkynes due to the absence of double or triple bonds.
 
• Alkanes are found in natural gas and petroleum and are used as fuels and solvents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkynes**:

 
 
• These are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C).
 
• The general formula for alkynes is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
 
• Examples include ethyne (acetylene) C₂H₂.
 
 
 
• **Ethylene**:
 
 
• Also known as ethene, it is an unsaturated hydrocarbon with the formula C₂H₄.
 
• Ethylene contains a carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).
 
• It is widely used in the chemical industry, particularly in the production of polyethylene.
 
 
 
• **Alkenes**:
 
 
• These are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).
 
• The general formula for alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ.
 
• Examples include ethene (C₂H₄) and propene (C₃H₆).
 
 
 
• **Saturation and Unsaturation**:
 
 
• Saturated compounds have single bonds between carbon atoms, making them more stable and less reactive.
 
• Unsaturated compounds have double or triple bonds between carbon atoms, which makes them more reactive.
 
• Hydrogenation is the process of converting unsaturated compounds to saturated ones by adding hydrogen.
